evidence.claim: Police repressed 93 people, mostly female students from Mactumactzá; Amnesty reported excessive force, racist/classist/misogynistic insults, sexual-violence threats, and psychological torture during detention.
evidence.title: The right to protest is under threat in Mexico
evidence.excerpt: Police repressed 93 people, mostly female students from Mactumactzá; Amnesty reported excessive force, racist/classist/misogynistic insults, sexual-violence threats, and psychological torture during detention.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous human-rights reporting with detailed victim accounts.
evidence.period_fit: Adjacent to the target year; it documents the protest climate shaping 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: the abuse was by state police under AMLO-era governance, not a direct federal order evidenced here.
contrary_evidence: The incident was handled by state police rather than the federal executive.
It is one incident, not by itself a nationwide pattern.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that President López Obrador intensified immigration restrictions and enforcement, including new visa requirements and domestic-status checks; soldiers and immigration agents ran checkpoints, and the Mexican Supreme Court had ruled those checkpoints unconstitutional.
evidence.title: Mexico: Asylum Seekers Face Abuses at Southern Border
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that President López Obrador intensified immigration restrictions and enforcement, including new visa requirements and domestic-status checks; soldiers and immigration agents ran checkpoints, and the Mexican Supreme Court had ruled those checkpoints unconstitutional.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Investigative human-rights report based on interviews, documents, and corroborating evidence.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 evidence based on interviews extending into May 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: these were executive policy choices and enforcement practices under AMLO.
contrary_evidence: Some officials framed the policy as migration control rather than coercion.
The Supreme Court ruling provides a legal check, not proof of executive compliance.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said that on 31 August 2022 President López Obrador proposed reforms to place the National Guard under the military control of Sedena, allow active military personnel to serve without leaving their military posts, send alleged human-rights crimes to military courts, and require military training for all National Guard personnel.
evidence.title: Mexico: Militarization of public security will lead to more human rights violations and perpetuate impunity
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said that on 31 August 2022 President López Obrador proposed reforms to place the National Guard under the military control of Sedena, allow active military personnel to serve without leaving their military posts, send alleged human-rights crimes to military courts, and require military training for all National Guard personnel.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous advocacy response quoting the executive proposal and its key provisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct AMLO attribution: this was his proposal.
contrary_evidence: Supporters argued the change would improve security coordination.
The proposal itself does not prove every downstream abuse, but it does show a militarizing choice.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that the special prosecutor resigned in September 2022, the attorney general had been obstructing the Ayotzinapa investigation by refusing warrants and forensic work and by intervening to cancel warrants against military and government officials, and that a presidential ally with no human-rights investigation experience was appointed to replace him.
evidence.title: Obstruction Threatens Probe into Disappeared Mexico Students
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that the special prosecutor resigned in September 2022, the attorney general had been obstructing the Ayotzinapa investigation by refusing warrants and forensic work and by intervening to cancel warrants against military and government officials, and that a presidential ally with no human-rights investigation experience was appointed to replace him.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed contemporaneous analysis with specific institutional actions and named actors.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but substantial: the case involved presidential orders, military resistance, and the AMLO administration's handling of accountability.
contrary_evidence: HRW also notes that August 2022 saw 83 arrest warrants, showing real earlier progress.
This is a case-specific accountability failure, not proof of generalized nationwide terror.

evidence.claim: UN human-rights staff said leaked Sedena documents or a government-acquired software package revealed illicit surveillance against journalists and human-rights defenders, calling it grave, intimidating, and contrary to a safe environment for criticism.
evidence.title: La ONU-DH expresa su preocupación por actos de vigilancia ilícita contra personas defensoras de derechos humanos y periodistas
evidence.excerpt: UN human-rights staff said leaked Sedena documents or a government-acquired software package revealed illicit surveillance against journalists and human-rights defenders, calling it grave, intimidating, and contrary to a safe environment for criticism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN country-office statement with explicit concern about government-linked surveillance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: it implicates federal authorities and the armed forces under AMLO.
contrary_evidence: The statement is not itself a court finding of personal presidential orders.
It addresses surveillance/intimidation more than kinetic violence.

evidence.claim: The presidency said AMLO's commitment was to tell the truth, that 41,168 documents had been reviewed, the report and annexes were public, three students had been identified, and there were sufficient elements to continue investigating 33 people.
evidence.title: Rinde informe presidencia de la Comisión para la Verdad y Acceso a la Justicia en el caso Ayotzinapa
evidence.excerpt: The presidency said AMLO's commitment was to tell the truth, that 41,168 documents had been reviewed, the report and annexes were public, three students had been identified, and there were sufficient elements to continue investigating 33 people.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential statement with concrete accountability steps and document totals.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct AMLO-cabinet accountability and transparency effort, though it concerns a historical atrocity rather than a current incident.
contrary_evidence: This is about a 2014 crime, not a broad fix for 2022 violence.
Later obstruction allegations complicate the picture.

evidence.claim: The UN communication concerns the killings of Esmeralda Gallardo Sánchez and María del Carmen Vázquez, two women searchers, in a context of growing attacks against relatives and collectives searching for disappeared people in Mexico.
evidence.title: Mexico - MEX 14/2022
evidence.publisher: Special Procedures of the Human Rights Council
evidence.excerpt: The UN communication concerns the killings of Esmeralda Gallardo Sánchez and María del Carmen Vázquez, two women searchers, in a context of growing attacks against relatives and collectives searching for disappeared people in Mexico.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN communications database, but the item is an allegation/concern summary rather than a merits finding.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: it highlights failures of state protection for search collectives under the AMLO administration.
contrary_evidence: The communication records alleged information, not adjudicated findings.
It speaks to a protection gap rather than direct presidential order.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 evidence on AMLO's personal control over civilian-nuclear safety appointments, regulatory discipline, or command-side decisions is thin.
There is no Mexico-originating war, proxy conflict, or coercive peace leverage in 2022, so the dossier is mostly diplomatic posture rather than operational conflict conduct.
Specific chain-of-command evidence for some police, military, and intelligence abuses remains incomplete, especially for local versus federal responsibility.
Some of the evidence about electoral reform and media pressure is rhetorical or journalistic rather than a direct legal finding of intent to entrench power.
The causal split between AMLO policy, inherited weakness, and global shocks is still only partially recoverable for 2022 poverty, inflation, and investment outcomes.
Independent post-launch quality and outcome audits for IMSS-Bienestar, education recovery, and related welfare programs are thinner than the rollout record.
Direct documentary evidence of personal enrichment, hidden financial benefit, or knowing approval of surveillance remains limited.
Durability and post-launch independent audits for AIFA, Dos Bocas, IMSS-Bienestar, and the education programs are thinner than the implementation record.
